key_insight: Independent price-based scheduling of EVs and heat pumps can synchronize flexible demand and create feeder peaks that exceed uncoordinated operation.
engineering_relevance: Distribution-grid operators need coordination or transformer-aware control, because local cost optimization alone can worsen voltage and thermal loading on low-voltage feeders.
method: Simulated a rural low-voltage feeder with 97 buses and a 250 kVA transformer.
Ran 160 simulations across seven scenarios, four seasons, and 0–90% penetration of EVs, heat pumps, and PV.
Compared decentralized price minimization with fixed schedules and a centralized transformer-capped schedule.
evidence_signal: At 30% EV and heat-pump penetration, price-based scheduling pushed the transformer to 253% of rated capacity, with up to 478% at 90% EV penetration, while the evaluation also identified first undervoltage violations at the far end of the feeder.
watch_item: Results are feeder- and scenario-dependent, so deployment needs local validation and may be constrained by midday PV reverse-power-flow limits.
paper_title: Price-Optimized EV and Heat-Pump Scheduling Can Exceed Uncoordinated Feeder Peaks
